We ran it through Kilo Code (the VS Code extension) on a real backend task to see how it handles planning, implementation, and the long tool-calling sequence in between. TL;DR: Grok Build 0.1 planned and built a working webhook delivery service in TypeScript, Bun, and SQLite for $1.65 total ($0.17 to plan, $1.48 to implement) at roughly 120 tokens per second, with zero tool-calling failures across the run.
